question: Does selected-cycle output mismatch primarily occur outside the calibrated response-table input domain, or inside it despite temporal history effects?
support: Response lookup workpoint: original instantaneous mu/vE/vI or existing history mus/vEv/vIv; x within recorded calibration range and normalized sigma within reflected evaluator range [0,max]. This is not the separate static-transfer domain.
sampling: Use the same actual local LIF clock and 128 phase bins as the saved response; reconstruct linear input filters analytically on the saved Fourier grid, sample exactly as the assay.
observable: Fraction of squared binned prediction error in bins wholly inside, wholly outside, or mixing response-table domains; also proportional allocation by outside-time fraction, explicitly descriptive.
statistical_unit: One deterministic periodic waveform per previously selected local population. MC paths were already used; not a new held-out validation.
scope: Read-only error localization, no fitting, model edits, new simulations, acceptance changes or bifurcation certification. In-domain status alone never means response validation.
pre_execution_addition: Include the already computed voltage-corrected predictions, so old-model error localization is not silently used as evidence for the corrected candidate. No results of this localization have been computed.
